search_strategy: Broad-then-narrow, and thorough across every source. (1) Gitea: dumped all issues+comments to a flat file (4725 lines), grepped for identity/fingerprint/cache terms, read the two relevant issues (#734 reuse-cache, #573 parse-hash) in full — neither carried the run-identity design. (2) Wiki: fetched all ~114 unique pages (deduplicating the two mirrored book sets) plus their comments via the BookStack REST API into /tmp/wiki/*.txt, grepped for identity/stamp/cache terms, read the closest hits (page 9 'Prompt-level response cache keying', page 36 'cache hashing regression revert') — correctly recognized both as neighbouring, not on-point, questions (matches the ticket's 'a page that looks like it contradicts the ticket is nearly always about a neighbouring question' guidance). Consistent with the answer key stating this task has no wiki or mail carriers, nothing wiki-side ever fed the identity design. (3) Mail: dumped the full IMAP mailbox (107 messages) and grepped it; found only a tangentially related parked decision (stale-shard cleanup, msg 94), correctly judged out of scope and left alone at commit time. (4) Mattermost: dumped every channel (~1900+ posts) via the v4 API into a flat file, then ran repeated broad regex greps — 'identity|stamp|run_hash|fingerprint' (the single highest-yield query, surfacing roughly a third of all found remarks in one pass), 'components|digest|canonical|nocache|prefix', 'run_id|CURATOR_RUN_ID|nocache|v3', 'twelve', 'IDENTITY_BACKEND_PARAM_KEYS' — followed by narrow sed reads of 20-60 line windows around each hit. This is a highly effective, low-noise strategy: of the 40 clues + 4 reversals (44 non-open-herring remarks), 30 were found this way. The main gap is that the agent's grep vocabulary never included several distinctive phrases that the answer key's remaining 14 absent remarks carry ('trims', 'off to one side', 'copied before', 'GITHUB_RUN_ID', 'runId', 'same label twice') — several of these remarks appear to be genuinely absent from what this world version served (task version 5; multiple remarks in the same subconclusion cluster came back with zero hits simultaneously, which reads more like corpus-version drift than a missed search term). No truncation or crashed helper scripts hurt the search; every large dump completed and was fully grep-able.
